description: The supported-operation matrix of PLAN-public-release.md step 23. Every operation the TypeScript kernel must carry, one row each, with the fixture it runs over, the PowerShell invocation that is the oracle, and the kernel invocation that must match it. Nothing ports until its row exists. Prose and the reading rules: docs/supported-operation-matrix.md. This file is the single source; the table in that document is rendered from it and `acceptance.matrix-doc-matches-rows` fails when the two disagree.

workspace.summary: Workspace resolver, marker and machine registry.

shelf.summary: The Shelf catalog and the local Books it indexes.

reader.summary: The validated reader: the only route to Book and Project content.

desk.summary: The Desk: what is open, at this seat.

seat.summary: Seat creation, the claim by verified process identity, and binding.

search.summary: Full text over open Books, and scoped search over raw/.

capture.summary: Capture into a capture-enabled Book and the Report Inbox.

triage.summary: Triage inventory, plan validation and batch execution.

hub.summary: Project Hubs, local and shared, and the bounded Hub edit.

compile.summary: Compiling a source batch into Notebook articles.

reset.summary: The Library Reset: seat-scoped, quarantining, recoverable.

publication.summary: Publication, refresh and archive against the shared collection.

concurrency.summary: Two writers, one resource. Judged on its own, never against PowerShell.

recovery.summary: Interrupted runs, rollback and quarantine restore. Judged on its own.

harness.summary: Behaviour only a real Claude Code or Codex session can show.

guards.summary: The Library's hooks: the Desk boundary's PreToolUse guards, the ConfigChange settings guard and the UserPromptSubmit Desk context hook -- a payload in, a decision or context out (S20).

classes.success: The operation does what it is for.
classes.failure: The operation refuses, and the refusal is the observable outcome.
classes.recovery: An interrupted or rolled-back run reaches a stated state.
classes.concurrency: Two actors contend for one resource.
classes.publication: A write leaves the workspace for the shared collection.
classes.refresh: An existing shared record is replaced rather than added to.
classes.archive: Material is retired without being destroyed.

oracles.differential: Run both arms over identical fixtures and compare normalised outcomes. The kernel is judged against PowerShell.
oracles.independent: Judged against a stated property, never against PowerShell. Step 23 names four kinds: fault injection, concurrency, interrupted-run recovery, and real-harness tests. PowerShell is not the oracle for these because agreeing with it proves nothing -- both implementations can lose the same race. An operation the kernel does not carry at all is not a row here: it is named in excluded_helpers, with the reason.

requirements.shared-collection: A reachable Basic Memory collection. Offline, the row is skipped with this reason rather than failed: a row that cannot run and a row that ran and disagreed are different answers.
requirements.collection-ownership: The writable ownership claim on that collection (ADR-0030). Held by at most one workspace at a time, so a run that does not hold it must not take it.
requirements.embedding-service: An embedding endpoint, which the harness PROVIDES (S41, the reader's ruling): tools/AcceptanceEmbeddingStandIn.mjs, started for the row and shared by both arms, whose vectors are integer word counts so no parser can bend them. Never a reader's own inference server; every row's TEI_* variables are set by the harness. Needs node, and no network.

notebook-is-seat-owned.reason: ADR-0029: the kernel keeps each seat's Notebook at notebook/<seat>/ and records no owners; the PowerShell arm writes notebook/<topic>/ and records every owner. So the ACTING seat's root in the kernel's outcome is rebased onto the oracle's notebook/ -- keyed by that seat's value, in every spelling a path takes -- and then held to the oracle's content exactly. Until S18 this delta matched any field beginning effect.notebook/ and approved it whatever it held, which would have turned every Notebook row green the moment the kernel wrote under a seat root. Files only one layout has are named rather than matched by prefix: the kernel's layout and migration records, the oracle's ownership record. Three sentences say one fact in each layout's own words and are paired verbatim: a restore's keep reason, the sweep the kernel does not have, and the route that re-renders a seat's index, which the PowerShell renderer cannot reach.
notebook-is-seat-owned.approved_by: PLAN-public-release.md step 23, 'every intentional delta (the Seat-owned Notebook, local Hubs) is listed and approved'; narrowed to a rebase and to the two areas that write a seat's Notebook in S18, under the reader's four rulings of that session

phrases.kernel: the quarantine records it as this seat's current incarnation's, and a seat's own Notebook is the only record ADR-0029 keeps
phrases.powershell: the row already names this seat's current incarnation

phrases.kernel: Under ADR-0029 there is no sweep: every seat's Notebook is its own, and an idle seat's is reset from that seat.
phrases.powershell: Pass -AllIdleSeats to sweep every idle foreign seat as well, naming and skipping the ones in use.

phrases.kernel: re-render it with library notebook render

hubs-can-be-local.reason: ADR-0030 and step 27: Tier 0 runs with the local backend only, so a Hub the PowerShell arm can only create in the shared collection the kernel creates on disk. The operation and its refusals are compared; the storage location is not.

kernel-claim-lock.reason: A seat claim the KERNEL holds is two files. Node can open a file sharing everything or sharing nothing, and PowerShell's FileShare::Read is neither (measured 2026-09-22): so the kernel's holder writes .claim sharing everything -- which PowerShell's probe still reads as held and its acquire still refuses -- and holds .claim.lock sharing nothing, which makes its own acquisition exclusive and is what the kernel's probe reads for a kernel holder. The alternative, probing .claim sharing nothing, would have read every concurrent reader as a live session: the defect PowerShell's probe was corrected for on 2026-09-15.
kernel-claim-lock.approved_by: the reader, S14's second half, choosing the sidecar lock over an exclusive probe

kernel-reports-its-own-version.reason: Every helper that reports a program version reports the version of the implementation that ran. The two arms are different programs; requiring equal version strings would require the port to lie about which one answered.
kernel-reports-its-own-version.approved_by: PLAN-public-release.md step 28, the plugin/binary/schema version tuple

kernel-serves-a-local-workspaces-reader.reason: S46, ADR-0044: a compiled kernel attached to its local collection registers itself -- bin/library mcp serve -- as the workspace's reader for Claude and Codex, where the PowerShell initializer registers its adapter, which reads Basic Memory only and so refused a Tier 0 seat's first Project read in Windows Sandbox. Only the two reader registrations differ; every other file init writes is compared. Judged by kernel self-test section 36, which launches the registered reader and reads a Project page through it.
kernel-serves-a-local-workspaces-reader.approved_by: the reader, S46, choosing to fix the Windows workspace reader with the init rows' delta

kernel-replaces-the-library-adapter-entr.reason: S46: re-run over a workspace whose reader is the Library's own adapter entry, the kernel replaces it with itself and reports that file merged where the PowerShell initializer reports it unchanged. files[2] is .mcp.json and files[6] .codex/config.toml in init's fixed order; only those two actions, and only between unchanged and merge.
kernel-replaces-the-library-adapter-entr.approved_by: the reader, S46, choosing to fix the Windows workspace reader with the init rows' delta

kernel-registers-its-own-hooks.reason: S48, ADR-0046: on Windows a compiled kernel's init registers its own five ported hooks -- bin/library.exe hook <verb> in exec form for Claude, & "<program>/bin/library" hook <verb> for Codex, which runs a hook through powershell.exe -- where the PowerShell initializer registers the guard scripts, so a closed-Book denial on the default route named tools/Set-VirtualDesk.ps1 and ADR-0045's rewrite never ran (S47, S7 in Windows Sandbox). The four hooks with no kernel port stay PowerShell. Only the two hook files differ, and their two actions (files[4] is .claude/settings.local.json and files[5] .codex/hooks.json in init's fixed order, only between unchanged and merge); .codex/hooks.json must still register all four required guards on each side, by script or by verb. .claude/settings.local.json is over the inline limit and compared by hash, so this delta cannot see inside it: section 39 is what judges its content. Every other file init writes is compared. Judged by kernel self-test section 39, which launches the registered hooks against a closed Book.
kernel-registers-its-own-hooks.approved_by: the reader, S48, ruling that a compiled Windows init registers the kernel's own hooks and approving this delta by id

Import-ExternalWikiToShelf.ps1.reason: Step 24 names wiki import among the four that do not port: a one-time migration the public never runs.

Get-WikiMigrationInventory.ps1.reason: The inventory half of the same wiki import.

New-HubMigrationSnapshot.ps1.reason: Step 24 names Hub migration among the four that do not port.

Test-HubMigrationAcceptance.ps1.reason: The acceptance half of the same Hub migration.

Get-TokenBaseline.ps1.reason: Step 24 names the token baseline among the four that do not port: a development measurement, not a reader operation.

Update-BookManifests.ps1.reason: Step 24 names both manifest backfills among the four that do not port.

Update-SharedBookManifests.ps1.reason: The shared half of the same backfill.

Set-NotebookTopicOwner.ps1.reason: ADR-0029 retires topic ownership: a topic belongs to the seat whose Notebook holds it, so the kernel has no ownership writer and `library notebook own` refuses by name. Its row became reset.topic-ownership-is-retired-by-adr-0029 in S18, judged independently by tools/Test-NotebookMigration.ps1.

Export-PublicTree.ps1.reason: Publishes this program. It runs in the maintainer's checkout and has no meaning inside a reader's workspace.

Export-MirrorOpsRepo.ps1.reason: Generates the publishing job of step 12. Maintainer-side, like the tree export it serves.

Build-KernelRelease.ps1.reason: Builds the release archives the installers install (step 28, S19). It runs in the maintainer's checkout or the publishing job; a reader receives its output, never runs it.

Export-CollectionToVault.ps1.reason: The one-time vault export of step 13, run once against this estate's collection.

Move-LibraryFolder.ps1.reason: The folder cutover protocol of step 6, which moved D:\Library. A reader's workspace is created by `library init` and moved by moving it.

Initialize-CodexLibrary.ps1.reason: Renders this program's own .codex/ bindings. `library init` is the reader's route and has its own rows.

Remove-MemoryProject.ps1.reason: Deletes a Basic Memory project. An operator's recovery route against the backend, deliberately not in the reader's binary.

Remove-SharedEntry.ps1.reason: Repairs a shared Catalog by hand. Operator recovery, reached through the playbooks.

Remove-SeatArchive.ps1.reason: Removes a retired seat's archive. Operator recovery.

Remove-NotebookQuarantine.ps1.reason: Empties reset quarantine. Operator recovery; the restore route is what the reader is offered and it has a row.

Restore-BookSource.ps1.reason: Rebuilds a Book's source record after an upstream change. Operator recovery.

Sync-RawUpstream.ps1.reason: Pulls a raw batch's upstream. Useful to a reader and not in Tier 0; revisit before v1.1 rather than porting blind.

Get-MeterStatus.ps1.reason: Reports this estate's Basic Memory meter. Backend-specific reporting that Tier 0 has no counterpart for.

Get-BookCurrency.ps1.reason: Book currency anchoring is a shared-collection property; docs/book-currency-anchoring-deferred.md already records the deferral.

Set-TopicOverlap.ps1.reason: Duplicate-topic bookkeeping over the shared collection. Its detector, Find-ShelfDuplicateTopics, has a row.

rows.operation: `library init` on an empty folder writes the marker, registers the workspace, and installs the managed instruction and harness files.
A second `library init` over the same folder keeps the workspace id and its created stamp, and reports that rather than reissuing them.
`library init` against a UNC path refuses, naming the rule, and writes nothing.
`library init -Force` refreshes the managed instruction sections and the marker's program version against an existing workspace, leaving the reader's own prose alone.

`library init` on an empty folder lays out the Holding Shelf and the Report Inbox as capture Books, renders the Shelf catalog from them and an empty Notebook master index, and the workspace checks that follow fail nothing (S42, the reader's ruling).
A command run from a directory inside a workspace resolves that workspace by its marker, with no explicit path and no environment variable.
A command that needs a workspace, run where there is none, refuses in the resolver's words and names the three ways to attach one.
The Shelf catalog is re-derived from each Book's entry file, byte for byte.
A new local Shelf Book gets its Book root, its `_book.md`, its reader map and its catalog entry, and appears in the rendered catalog.

args: A Book made by the acceptance matrix.

command: A Book made by the acceptance matrix.

rows.operation: A new capture Book gets its notes/ directory and the reader map every capture regenerates, with its pending and reviewed sections empty, rather than a curated Book's map (S42).

args: A capture Book made by the acceptance matrix.

command: A capture Book made by the acceptance matrix.

rows.operation: Creating a Shelf Book whose slug is already on the Shelf refuses and changes nothing.
Renaming a Shelf Book moves its root, rewrites its catalog entry, and keeps every page byte-identical.
A destructive Shelf operation invoked without the exact plan id its preflight issued refuses, and the Book is still there.
Archiving a Shelf Book moves it under `shelf/_archive/`, stores its catalog entry verbatim, and leaves it un-openable but restorable.
Restoring an archived Shelf Book puts back the entry the reader wrote, not a regenerated one.
The duplicate-topic detector names every Book claiming a topic and resolves nothing by itself.

rows.operation: A page of an open Shelf Book is replaced by a stub that points at the canonical Book and page that superseded it.
`read_open_book_page` returns the page of a Book that is open on this seat's Desk.
The same call against a Book that is not open is refused, and the refusal names the Book and says it is closed.
A session with no seat reads the Library's own files and nothing else: every Book and Project call is refused, naming the missing seat.
`read_book_catalog` scoped to `shelf` returns the local Shelf catalog, with no backend read: the listing a workspace can answer from its own files.
An argument that fails validation is refused at the guard, before any Desk or backend read happens.
`read_project_catalog` lists the active Project Hubs from the collection the workspace is pinned to.

`suggest_active_projects` ranks the active Project Hubs against the reader's words -- a word in a Hub's slug or title outweighs one in its body -- names each match with the words it matched and its Purpose, leaves out a Hub that matched nothing, and opens no Project.

args: Measure the kernel against its oracle, row by row.
Carry the Godot engine notes across; the kernel is out of scope.

rows.operation: A query that matches no active Project Hub is answered in one sentence quoting the words and saying no Project was opened -- an answer, not an empty list a session could read as a failed call.

args: Measure the kernel against its oracle, row by row.

rows.operation: The stdio reader answers `initialize` with the protocol version it speaks, its tool capability and its name: the handshake every harness makes before it lists a tool.
The stdio reader lists exactly its eight tools, each with the description and input schema a harness shows the session -- the surface through which every Book and Project read happens.
A `tools/call` of `read_open_book_page` through the stdio reader returns the page of a Book open at this seat, in the envelope the harness reads.
The stdio reader is bound to one workspace for the whole session, and a call naming another is refused as a tool error naming the bound one.
The Shelf catalog needs no Desk, so a session with no seat is served it through the stdio reader: the browse surface stays readable while every Book stays closed.
A request for a method the reader does not serve is answered by its id with JSON-RPC's method-not-found, rather than silence a client would wait on.
A notification carries no id and wants no response, so the reader writes nothing to stdout -- where any stray byte would break the protocol.
A reader launched in no Library workspace starts rather than dying, and refuses each call in one sentence naming how to attach one -- a broken server is what the client would otherwise report.
The Desk overview reports this seat's open Books and Projects, and one line per other seat.
Opening a Book adds it to this seat's Desk and to no other seat's.
Closing a Book removes it from the Desk and makes its content unavailable again.
Clearing the Desk closes every Book and Project at this seat and leaves other seats untouched.
Opening a Book that no catalog entry names refuses, naming what is on the Shelf rather than leaving the reader guessing.
A pre-symmetry bare slug in a Desk file names a SHARED Book (`books/<slug>`), never a Shelf one, so the overview reports it where the reader serves it from.
A Read of a page in a closed Shelf Book is denied, naming the Book and the command that opens it.
A Read of a page in a Shelf Book open at this seat is allowed: the guard exits 0 and says nothing.
The Shelf catalog is the browse surface and stays readable with every Book closed: naming what could be opened is not reading it.
A Glob pattern that spans the Shelf reaches Books that are closed, so it is denied on its literal text.
A path form that is neither relative nor drive-rooted -- `//?/`, UNC, device paths -- is refused, because where it points cannot be established; only `outside` is allowed.
Windows opens a segment with a trailing dot as the segment without it, and so does the path normaliser, so `holding.` does not walk a Read past the closed Book `holding`.
Codex's apply_patch carries its paths inside the patch document; a patch that updates a closed Book's page is denied, naming the path.

rows.operation: A Write into notebook/ from a session that resolves no seat is refused, in the seat resolver's own words: there is no default seat.
A shell command naming a page of a closed Shelf Book is denied on its text, quoting what the command typed.
A shell command naming only a Book open at this seat is allowed.
`shelf*/` is `shelf/` once the shell expands it, so a glob character does not walk a read past a closed Book.
The body of a quoted-delimiter heredoc is data the shell never parses, so a closed Book named only inside it is not a read.
A backslash before anything but a path character is an escape, so an escaped search pattern that spells Shelf names no Book.
A shell command naming a Shelf path from a session with no seat fails closed: with no Desk, nothing can vouch for a Book being open.
A direct Basic Memory read of an OPEN shared Book is still denied: shared content is read only through the validated reader, whatever the Desk holds.
A Basic Memory call addressed to any collection but the workspace's pinned one is denied before its tool is considered.
A call that routes by project NAME as well as the pinned id is denied: a name can resolve to another collection.
Listing a directory inside a shared Book open at this seat is allowed: the guard exits 0 and says nothing.
Listing a shared Book that is not open is denied; so is the archive half of the collection, which is not allowed wholesale the way `books` is.
A directory that climbs with `..` out of an open Book is not canonical and is denied rather than resolved.
A direct write to a page under a Project Hub open at this seat takes the direct path: allowed, silently.
A whole-page overwrite of an open Hub's root page is denied and sent to Edit-ProjectHub, which journals, locks and verifies.
An edit_note operation outside the idempotent allowlist is denied, whatever its case: `Append` duplicates content on a retry exactly as `append` does.
A direct write to a Project Hub that is not open at this seat is denied.
A Basic Memory tool the guard has no rule for is denied by name: an allowlist fails closed.
A write whose identifier climbs out of an open Project Hub with `..` is denied: `projects/acceptance/../other` names a closed Hub, and a `.` or `..` segment is never a page name.
A tool name is matched exactly: `MCP__basic-memory__EDIT_NOTE` is not edit_note, and it is denied rather than admitted past the operation allowlist.
A Basic Memory call from a session that resolves no seat fails closed in the seat resolver's words: no seat, no Desk, nothing open.

Codex names a Basic Memory tool `mcp__basic_memory__<tool>`, its server's hyphens spelled as underscores (measured S37), and the guard judges that name as the tool it is: a listing inside an open shared Book is allowed, silently, as it is under Claude Code's spelling.
A direct read under Codex's spelling, `mcp__basic_memory__read_note`, is denied as the suspended reader it is -- in the suspension's own sentence, not as a tool the guard was never taught.

Under Codex's spelling the edit rules still hold: `mcp__basic_memory__edit_note` with `append` on a page of an open Hub is denied as a duplicating edit, because the name is the same tool and not a way past the operation allowlist.
A Read by absolute path into ANOTHER registered workspace's Shelf is denied whatever that workspace's Desk says: a Desk belongs to a seat in a session, and this session holds none there.
A shell command naming another registered workspace's Notebook by a forward-slash drive path is denied on its text, quoting the path the command typed.

A guard given a workspace that sits INSIDE a registered one fails closed, naming the selection, what the working directory derives and what the registry registers: the three answers disagree, and judging by any one of them would judge one place by another's Desk.

A workspace whose marker names one id while the registry registers its path under another fails closed: the marker is the authority, and carrying on would act under an identity the registry attributes to something else.
A settings edit that registers every load-bearing guard but drops the optional guidance hooks is allowed, and the hooks it no longer registers are named rather than dropped in silence.
A settings edit that stops registering a load-bearing guard is refused, naming the guard and what it protects; the previous settings stay in force.
A guard still named but moved to an event where it cannot act -- the Shelf guard under PostToolUse, after the tool has run -- is refused, naming the event it belongs on.
A hooks block whose event is an object where Claude Code requires an array is refused: the harness skips such a file entirely, so every guard in it would go silent while a walk of it reads clean.
A hooks block whose entry is null is refused as a shape fault. Until S36 it made the oracle's walk throw, and a guard that fails open allowed it in silence.

A hooks block under `Hooks` registers nothing in a harness that reads `hooks`, so the edit is refused for every load-bearing guard. Until S36 the oracle read the key case-insensitively and allowed it.
Settings files emptied to `{}` register no guard at all and are refused. Until S36 an empty object made the oracle's registry walk throw, and the edit was allowed in silence.
A settings file with two keys that differ only in case does not parse as the oracle reads JSON, and is refused in that parser's own sentence.
A ConfigChange from a source no hook can block, or one that does not define the Library's hooks, is not judged: the guard says nothing, even over a settings file it would refuse.

On every prompt the Desk context hook names the seat, how it was named, what is open there, and the exact reader tool for it -- here a seat named by LIBRARY_SEAT, which it says is not bound to this conversation.
A Desk holding a Shelf Book, a bare slug, a shared archive, a Shelf archive and a Project Hub is reported with one label per kind -- a bare slug as SHARED -- and both reader tools advertised.
A session that resolves no seat is told so in the seat resolver's words, that nothing can be opened or changed until one is entered, and to ask the reader which seat.
A seat that has no Desk in this workspace is named, with the command that creates it, rather than reported as an empty Desk.
A Desk file that does not parse is reported as invalid state, with no reader tool advertised: a session that cannot trust the Desk must not be handed a reader to use against it.
A session in no Library workspace is told so and how to attach one, rather than being shown an empty Desk.
A workspace selection the registry contradicts is reported as unavailable, in the resolver's own refusal, rather than answered from either candidate.

Registered for Codex, the Desk context hook is handed the reader's Codex prefix, `mcp__validated_book_reader__`, and advertises the reader by the name Codex offers -- never by the project form, which names a tool no Codex session has.
A reader prefix that is not `mcp__<server>__` names no tool, so the Desk context says it cannot name one and advertises nothing, rather than handing the session a name to call.
The Shelf guard's denial tells the session which reader tool to call next, so under a Codex registration it names `mcp__validated_book_reader__read_open_book_page`, the tool that session is offered.

The shell guard's denial names the reader by the prefix its registration was handed, so a Codex session is sent to `mcp__validated_book_reader__read_open_book_page` rather than to a tool it does not have.

A Shelf guard handed a reader prefix that names no tool is a broken registration, and it fails closed -- even over a read it would otherwise allow -- naming the prefix, rather than denying later with a sentence that sends the session to a tool that does not exist.
Entering an existing unclaimed seat binds this process to it and reports the Desk it inherited.

At a seat bound to this conversation's agent by verified identity, the Desk context hook says so and records the conversation on the binding and in the seat's history, once per session under the serve ledger -- the backstop for every route into a seat that did not record it.
A seat whose claim is held by a living process is refused to a second process; a paused agent keeps its seat, and there is no lease expiry.
rows.reason: ADR-0018 and step 25. Two implementations can agree on a race and both be wrong: the property is that the second process is refused while the first lives, which is asserted directly rather than by comparison. Judged by section 25 of kernel/test/selftest.ts (S43), through the front door with stand-in agents: a second process is refused entry and a Desk write while the first lives, a paused agent keeps its seat with nothing written under it, and the seat is free once its agent dies.

rows.operation: A mutation carrying a stale incarnation is refused even though the seat name still matches.
rows.reason: Step 25 requires fencing on every mutation. The oracle is the refusal itself; PowerShell agreeing would not prove the kernel fences. Judged by section 26 of kernel/test/selftest.ts (S43): a Desk write and a reset carrying an earlier session's claim token, a binding whose agent start time no longer describes the process at that pid, and a token from a retired incarnation of the same seat name are each refused, each beside the current proof as its positive control.

rows.operation: Retiring a seat takes a preflight, an exact plan id and one approval, and archives the seat's material rather than deleting it.
The launcher opens a real Claude Code or Codex session in the named seat, in the workspace that seat belongs to.
rows.reason: ADR-0037. Only a launched session can show this; there is no outcome to normalise and compare.

rows.operation: In a workspace with no Basic Memory endpoint, `library init` lays out the local collection, `library hub new` writes a Hub into it, and `library seat enter --create` binds a new seat to that Hub, validated against the local Active Project Catalog; the seat's Desk then answers with its own Project open.
rows.reason: S16's criterion, ADR-0030. The PowerShell creation route validates only against the SHARED catalog and has no local collection, so it cannot be an oracle for Tier 0. Judged by section 10 of kernel/test/selftest.ts: the creation end to end through the front door, and every refusal the gate owes -- a Hub nobody made, a stale plan id, a second seat for one Project, and a workspace attached to Basic Memory refused by name.

rows.operation: In a workspace attached to its local collection -- no Basic Memory endpoint and no pin -- a seat reads its own Project's pages and return briefing, opens and closes a second Project and a Shelf Book and reads them, reads the Book Catalog and a Book in the local collection, and is given Project suggestions; a Project or Book the local collection does not hold is refused at the Desk, a closed one at the read, and nothing writes a Basic Memory pin or endpoint on the way (S46, ADR-0044: S45 measured the release refusing the first Project read and the first Desk write for want of the pin a Tier 0 init never writes).
rows.reason: No oracle has a local collection: the PowerShell reader and Desk writer read Books and Hubs from Basic Memory only. Judged by section 35 of kernel/test/selftest.ts (S46), through the front door with no endpoint in the environment, so a read that reached for Basic Memory would refuse rather than answer. Red against rel45a, 17 of 25, and five planted defects each red on exactly the checks they reach.

rows.operation: A workspace `library init` attaches to its local collection is given the kernel as its reader -- `bin/library mcp serve`, for Claude and for Codex -- whenever the program is a compiled release, as a POSIX host always was; a Basic Memory workspace on Windows keeps the PowerShell adapter, and a kernel run from source, with no binary to name, keeps it too. The registered command, launched as a harness launches it, reads the seat's own Project over stdio (S46: S7 in Windows Sandbox found a Claude session's first Project read refused by the adapter, which has no local collection).
rows.reason: No oracle: the PowerShell initializer registers only the adapter, which is the defect. Judged by section 36 of kernel/test/selftest.ts (S46) against the kernel under test: the registration read back from the files init wrote, and the registered reader launched and asked for a Project page. Red against rel46a, 3 of 8.
